parameters.name: min_samples_split
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of fitting samples required to split an internal node.

parameters.name: min_samples_leaf
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of fitting samples required in each leaf after a split.

parameters.name: min_weight_fraction_leaf
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of total fitting-sample weight required in a leaf.

parameters.name: max_features
parameters.meaning: Fraction of input features considered at each split.

parameters.name: min_impurity_decrease
parameters.meaning: Minimum weighted impurity decrease required for a split.

prior_facts: This random forest has a fixed ensemble of 10 trees; the six submitted controls govern tree growth and feature sampling.
Floating-point min_samples_split and min_samples_leaf become sample-count thresholds through ceil(fraction * number of samples fitted in the fold).
Without sample_weight, samples start with equal weights. min_weight_fraction_leaf constrains the fraction of total sample weight in each leaf.

Floating-point max_features becomes max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_)) features per split. Different inputs can select the same number of features. Finding a valid split may require inspecting more features than this number.
Depth, leaf size, minimum split size, and minimum impurity decrease jointly constrain tree growth.
background: Tune 6 hyperparameters of RandomForestRegressor on Diabetes Progression to reduce cross-validation prediction mean squared error.
input_instructions: Submit every parameter listed below, using its declared integer or floating-point type and inclusive bounds.

Submit original hyperparameter values. The transform column describes search coordinates, not a transformation to apply before submission: for example, submit 0.1 itself rather than log(0.1) or logit(0.1).
evaluation_details: The fixed split has 353 training and 89 held-out samples, with 10 features per sample. Feedback uses five-fold KFold cross-validation on the training split, with shuffle=False.
The objective is mean cross-validation squared prediction error on the released standardized regression target; lower is better.
Held-out results are not optimization feedback. No extra input scaling or preprocessing is added to the released arrays. Fixed estimator settings are listed below.
domain_knowledge: Deeper trees can fit finer patterns but can also overfit. Larger leaf and split thresholds restrict growth; evaluate their interactions rather than assuming maximum depth always helps.
